The '''spatial curvature parameter''', often denoted by $k$, models the spatial part of the [[spacetime]] curvature of the relativistic model of our [[Universe]]. It appears in various equations in [[cosmology]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Significance ==

Assuming [[the Cosmological Principle]], the [[Universe]] must be maximally symmetric, hence:

* $k=0$, the Universe is '''spatially flat''' and modelled correctly by a 3D [[Euclidean space]];
* $k<0$, the Universe can be modelled by a '''[[3-hyperboloid]]''';
* $k>0$, the Universe can be modelled by a '''[[3-sphere]] with finite volume'''.
